description: IDOR in a profile, record, or document endpoint. The backend accepts a user-supplied numeric ID (e.g. student_id, user_id, record_id) as a GET or POST parameter and returns data belonging to any user without verifying ownership. An authenticated attacker can enumerate IDs to access other users' private data.
exploit_hint: After logging in, change the user_id parameter from your own value (e.g. 42) to another user's ID (e.g. 43). The server should return the other user's data without authorization check.
requirements: The endpoint MUST accept a user_id (or equivalent) GET/POST parameter.
The backend MUST NOT verify that the session user matches the requested ID.
The response MUST include personal data (name, email, etc.) of the requested user.
Use sequential or guessable integer IDs (1, 2, 3...) to make enumeration trivial.
